steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Clave is a two-bar rhythmic pattern (3-2 or 2-3) that underpins virtually all Latin music — all other rhythmic parts align with the clave. | Key Fact: Bossa nova is a Brazilian style blending samba rhythms with jazz harmonies — gentle, syncopated guitar patterns and soft vocal delivery. | Key Fact: Salsa features piano montuno (repeated syncopated pattern), brass riffs, and layered percussion — it creates high-energy dance music through rhythmic complexity. | Key Fact: Tango and habanera share the distinctive rhythmic pattern (dotted quaver-semiquaver-quaver-quaver) — tango added dramatic expression and bandoneón.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how contemporary latin music are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use contemporary latin music. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use contemporary latin music in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
